newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU said to give 'positive signal' on Lonrho sale.
newsitem.headline: EU said to give 'positive signal' on Lonrho sale.

text.p: JCI Ltd, which wants to buy a stake in British conglomerate Lonrho Plc from Anglo American Corp of South Africa, has received signals the EU would approve the deal, a source at one of the companies said on Friday.

The source, who asked not to be identified, said JCI chairman MZI Khumalo had been "pretty much encouraged" at a recent meeting with the Commission's merger task force that the deal would not face any substantial opposition.
"I was told internally that when he came back from the Commission he was very happy," the source told Reuters.
The Commission declined to comment on his remark saying it was still investigating the transaction.

The Commission ordered mining firm giant Anglo American in April to reduce its holding in Lonrho to 9.99 percent from 27.5 percent due to fears it would leave the world's platinum market in the hands of two groups only -- Anglo/Lonrho and Gencor Ltd.
JCI took an option early July to buy 26.8 percent in Lonrho from Anglo for around 2.5 billion rand and Khumalo was quoted by Zimbabwean Financial Gazette on Thursday as saying the deal was sealed.

JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves said later Khumalo's comments should not imply the deal had already been cleared by the EU. Khumalo met with the director of the Commission's merger task force Goetz Drauz and other Commission officials on July 22 in Brussels.
The Commission warned in April the purchaser of Anglo's Lonrho stake must not be connected with Anglo or Gencor.

Immediately after the transaction was announced, Commission sources expressed concern about Anglo's representation on the JCI board and the fact Khumalo is an Anglo director and said the sale required a close look.

But the source, who has been following the negotiations in Brussels, said the crucial question was whether Anglo would be able to exercise a "decisive influence" on Lonrho Platinum through its stake in JCI. He did not believe it would be the case.

Anglo has about 18 percent of JCI. JCI would control almost 30 percent in Lonrho which owns 73 percent of its platinum division -- the rest belonging to Gencor. "It's a long shot. You cannot speak of decisive influence", he said.
According to the Commission, Anglo, Lonrho and Gencor together control 90 percent of the world reserves of platinum -- a precious metal used in the making of car catalytic converters.
